title: Curaprox (CURADEN AG)
meta: Built at aiconomy AG · lead contributor
summary: A full redesign of the Swiss and UAE Curaprox stores: two separate Shopify stores running from one shared base theme on Horizon.
details: Multi-store content system: blocks resolve their own content from the shop domain and from PIM metafields, so the same block renders UAE shipping copy on one store and Swiss copy on the other, and removes itself entirely when the backing metafield is empty.

A merchant-configurable product page accordion whose body is chosen by a source setting: rich text, a structured specification set from the PIM, ingredients or store-specific shipping information, with empty-value gating at every level.
Expert box block and the HubSpot newsletter integration, including a single language-independent form for the UAE store.
Store-aware social links, client-side blog filtering with OR-within-group logic and pagination, and a product card rating component.

title: EV Zug
meta: Built at aiconomy AG · lead contributor
summary: The official Shopify storefront of EV Zug, a Swiss National League hockey club: personalised jerseys, checkout bundling, live auctions and ERP-driven pricing.
details: Checkout bundling: a Cart Transform Function in TypeScript, compiled to WebAssembly, that merges personalised jersey components into a single bundle line in cart and checkout, keeping every component attached for fulfilment with no change to the total. Plus its admin page in the companion app.

Jersey personalisation: optical centering of jersey numbers using canvas-based glyph analysis, recalculated after the webfont loads, personalisation pricing, brand fonts and state that survives switching jerseys.
Live auction page with bidding interactions, modal flows and guest login.
Customer-specific pricing: aico ERP discount groups applied across product pages, product cards, quick add and cart, including Swiss Rappen rounding.
Bilingual DE/EN order confirmation emails in Outlook-safe Liquid.
Separate development and production themes on a branch-based workflow, with matching environments for the app.

title: Inuikii
meta: Built at aiconomy AG · lead contributor
summary: Four connected Shopify builds for the footwear brand: the main Swiss store, a private B2B showroom, an influencer store and a checkout app.
details: Search: Shopify's native search replaced with a Meilisearch storefront layer across search and collection pages, with colour grouping, market-aware pricing and instant results.

A back-in-stock and notify-me flow that replaced a paid third-party app, a size guide with per-product size scales, storewide sale pricing and a returns and refund-request flow driven by order tags and fulfilment status.
Virtual Showroom: a private B2B catalogue with prices, cart and checkout removed, and article numbers, size ranges and buyer-focused navigation added.
Influencer store: a private storefront with a Klaviyo integration that tags subscribers by store source.
Checkout app: a TypeScript Shopify app with an unsubscribe API and a Checkout UI extension showing editorial story cards in checkout and on the thank-you page.
Full DE/EN localisation.

title: Nile
meta: Built at aiconomy AG · lead contributor
summary: A Swiss fashion retailer running six Shopify stores from one shared theme: CHF, EUR and GBP, each with a test and a production store.
details: Loyalty program (Nilecard): a theme-driven points system with per-store redemption values, maximum points and fallback logic, plus points balance and history in the customer account.
Multi-store and localisation: the GBP store pair added to the build pipeline, cross-store country switching that remembers the shopper's choice, and per-store Klaviyo endpoints.
Customer account: order history and order detail with payment method and transaction breakdown.
Search: an InstantSearch implementation for the search page and predictive search, with progressive rendering and skeleton loading.
SEO: JSON-LD structured data for products, collections and breadcrumbs, including return policy, shipping and delivery-time data, with locale-aware schema and canonical URLs.

title: Ecofort
meta: Built at aiconomy AG · main developer
summary: Storefront for a Swiss supplier of heating and dehumidification products, plus theme repositories for the sister stores Infrarotheizung and Luftentfeuchter.
details: Performance: critical CSS extracted, theme scripts deferred, LCP image and fonts preloaded, and the product image slider rebuilt to remove layout shift on mobile.
An accessibility pass covering colour contrast, link names and iframe titles.
Collection loading with skeleton states, and an advice and news loader with per-article SEO, a 404 for empty pages and inactive articles filtered out.
Trusted Shops ratings, a delivery status indicator on the product page and legacy product IDs carried through cart into checkout for tracking.

Credit check reliability: Intrum outages were being treated as declines. The backend now reports whether Intrum actually returned a decision, calls have timeouts so checkout never hangs, and checkout shows a neutral "temporarily unavailable" message.

Header and search: a sticky gradient header with mega menu and mobile drawer, and predictive search across products, players and news in one modal.

Checkout bundling: a Cart Transform admin page and safety gate in the club's companion Shopify app.

Breadcrumbs, title, price and a transport and delivery-period block.

title: Chrüterhüsli
summary: Storefront for a Swiss drugstore and natural products retailer, built on Shopify's Horizon theme.
details: Wishlist, end to end: instead of browser storage, the client talks to a Shopify app proxy, so the list is held server side. Add, fetch, remove one and clear all are separate endpoints, and the button reconciles its state against the server on load so a saved item still reads as saved after a reload.
Every user-facing string comes from the theme's locale files with English fallbacks, so the feature stays translatable.
Contact page: the form and its confirmation flow.
Collection page: promotional image blocks with tablet-specific layout logic, the filter and results-count header, and product card alignment.
Blog list and article layouts, product page breadcrumbs and spacing, and DE/EN translation work.

title: Bruderer
summary: Storefront for a Swiss confectionery maker, with a custom product filtering layer that replaces Shopify's native facets.
details: A storefront filtering client that queries an external search service and builds its filters from product metafields: allergens, certifications and chocolate type.

Allergen normalisation: the same allergen appears under different spellings across the store's three languages and supplier data, so each one is reduced to a canonical name with an alias list. A shopper filtering on the German, English or French term lands on the same results.
The client resolves its own API endpoint from the shop domain, so production and staging each hit their own search index with no config change.
Customer login page, product page adjustments and DE/EN/FR translation work across the storefront.

title: Multi-store content sync
meta: Built at aiconomy AG · internal app
summary: An admin app that keeps content in sync across a client's multiple stores: metaobjects, metafields, menus, blogs, pages and translations. Deployed as a separate instance per client and built by a team of four developers.
details: Metaobject synchronisation: reserved Shopify types are checked for existence rather than created, definition validations are remapped against the target store, and referenced file IDs are mapped so images survive the transfer.
Blog metafields sync as a new route and UI, with deduplicated error summaries that expand to full detail.

Theme-referenced file backfill: enumerating a store's whole file library was timing out, so the app resolves only the files the live theme references and uploads those missing on the target, as a scheduled background job.
Exact-filename matching on file lookup, so naming collisions no longer upload the wrong asset.
Market adaptation, so each target store receives translations in its own primary language.

title: PrestaShop to Shopify migration app
meta: Built at aiconomy AG · internal app
summary: An admin app that migrates customers and historical orders from PrestaShop into Shopify through the Admin GraphQL API. Built once and run per market, first Switzerland and then the UAE.
details: The hard requirement was silence. Importing tens of thousands of historical customers and backdated orders into a live store would, by default, email every customer an account invitation and an order receipt.

The guarantee is enforced by the build: order creation is reachable through a single function that hardcodes the receipt options to false and bypasses inventory, customers are created without a password or invited state, and a guard test fails the build if the invite mutations are ever referenced.

A three-file upload stepper for the PrestaShop exports, with a dry run by default: parsed counts, per-file previews, unmatched customers, missing SKUs and blocked rows, all before anything is written.

Import is a separate action behind a confirmation that restates the no-email guarantee and the target shop domain. It runs customers then orders oldest first, reports live progress and can be cancelled.
Idempotent and resumable, so a failed run can be re-run safely, with a downloadable CSV report of every source row.
